extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory familiar with Mochizuki's IUT framework
extracted.subtask_description: A research paper (third in a series) developing the theory of the log-theta-lattice, log-links, log-shells, multiradial algorithms and the construction/estimation of splitting monoids of logarithmic Gaussian procession (LGP) monoids; aimed at constructing multiradial representations and log-volume estimates to be used in subsequent diophantine applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-link construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-link is obtained, roughly speaking, by applying, at each valuation v, the local pv-adic logarithm to the local units; it induces an isomorphism between the underlying D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters (Proposition 1.3, (i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be defined using the full ring structure (both additive and multiplicative structures) of local rings at v ∈ V; central for constructing log-shells; its definition depends essentially on ring structure, hence is not preserved by the non-ring/scheme-theoretic Θ-/Θ×μ-/Θ×μ_lgp-links. See Deﬁnition 1.1, Proposition 1.2 and Remark 1.4.1 for nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-shells (definition and containment property)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ Vbad, the log-shell at v is (roughly) the compact additive module Iv := p_v^{-1} · log_v(O×_{Kv}) ⊆ Kv ⊆ F_v (Definition 1.1, Remark 1.2.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log-shells must contain the images of the Kummer isomorphisms associated to both the domain and codomain of the log-link (O_{Kv} ⊆ Iv; log_v(O×_{Kv}) ⊆ Iv). There are functorial algorithms to construct mono-analytic/holomorphic and étale-like/Frobenius-like versions (Proposition 1.2 (v)-(ix)). Compatibility with log-volumes is crucial — leads to upper bounds in log-volume computations (Corollary 3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of coricity: vertical, horizontal, bi-coricity
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish coricity with respect to log-links (vertical coricity), coricity with respect to Θ-/Θ×μ-/Θ×μ_lgp-links (horizontal coricity), and coricity with respect to all arrows (bi-coricity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects intended for multiradial constructions should often be vertically coric (invariant with respect to vertical shifts via iterates of the log-link). Bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells are constructed using compatibility with F±-symmetry (Theorem 1.5) and play a central role in §3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariance under vertical shifts (vertical coricity) as a desideratum
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with objects in a vertical line of the log-theta-lattice that are invariant with respect to vertical shifts (i.e., shifts via iterates of the log-link) to allow constructions to translate across non-ring horizontal arrows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Étale-like objects that are vertically coric satisfy this invariance. Achieving invariance typically requires admitting some indeterminacy via log-Kummer correspondences; see Remarks 1.2.2(iii) and 1.4.1(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with F±-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-link and constructions must be compatible with the F±-symmetry which relates the various F-prime-strips and the labels appearing in Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compatibility produces vertically coric F×μ-prime-strips and bi-coric mono-analytic log-shells; it is used to synchronize conjugates and to enable Kummer theory relative to ring-theoretic basepoints (Remark 1.3.2, Theorem 1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism-class compatibility of mono-theta environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Mono-theta environments must satisfy 'isomorphism class compatibility' (compatibility with the topology of the tempered fundamental group), enabling the Kummer theory of mono-theta environments relative to ring-theoretic basepoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property is necessary to apply Kummer theory in log-Kummer correspondences and to ensure the conjugate synchronization arising from F±-symmetry is compatible with the log-link (Remark 2.1.1, [IUTchII] references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical splittings of theta/Gaussian monoids (up to roots of unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Canonical splittings (up to roots of unity) of theta/Gaussian monoids into unit group and value group portions exist and are used to relate multiplicative and additive structures across horizontal arrows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These canonical splittings are essential to (a) use value group portions to relate multiplicative structures across Θ-links and (b) use unit group portions shifted via a vertical arrow to relate additive structures; they are a formal consequence of cyclotomic/constant multiple rigidity (discussion preceding Theorem 3.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-Kummer correspondences and upper semi-compatibility (Ind3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Kummer isomorphisms between coric versions of data and other copies exist but are not compatible with coricity at the element level; this gives rise to 'upper semi-compatibility' (an indeterminacy labeled Ind3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The upper semi-compatibility (Ind3) is central: one typically only obtains vertically-invariant structures by admitting such indeterminacy; it underlies inequalities (upper bounds) in log-volume computations (Proposition 1.2 (iv), Theorem 3.11 (ii), Corollary 3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three admitted indeterminacies in multiradial representation (Ind1, Ind2, Ind3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiradial representations are constructed while admitting three types of indeterminacy: (Ind1) automorphisms/permutation automorphisms of processions/D-prime-strips; (Ind2) automorphisms of F×μ-prime-strips (the (Ẑ)×-indeterminacies on copies of O×μ); (Ind3) upper semi-compatibility arising from log-Kummer correspondences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indeterminacies are explicitly listed (Theorem 3.11, summarized in Theorem A); constructions, estimates and mutual-compatibility statements are made modulo these indeterminacies. One must track which aspects of the theory absorb or control each Ind(i) (e.g., holomorphic hulls, log-volumes, averaging/processions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference / mutual compatibility property
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiplicative monoids given by splitting monoids of LGP-monoids and copies of F×_mod 'do not interfere', relative to arrows in the log-Kummer correspondence, with the local units at v ∈ V that give rise to log-shells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formal non-interference follows for splitting monoids from the canonical splittings and for copies of F×_mod from algebraic number theory facts (elements integral everywhere are roots of unity). Theorem 3.11 (ii) and Theorem A (ii) detail these mutual compatibility properties which are used to separate multiplicative actions from unit-group log-shell phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic and constant-multiple rigidity (insulation from (Ẑ)×-indeterminacies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic and constant multiple rigidity requires only the torsion subgroup Oμ_{F_v}, and the triviality of certain composites insulates Kummer theory from (Ẑ)×-indeterminacies acting on copies of O×μ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rigidity is used in §2 multiradiality theory and in proving immunity of cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms to (Ẑ)× actions (discussion around Fig. I.3 and §2). It underpins the multiradial treatment of splitting monoids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-volume compatibility and estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Log-link compatibility with log-volumes is required; computations yield estimates (upper bounds) for log-volumes of LGP-monoids which are sufficient for later diophantine applications (Corollary 3.12, Theorem B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because log-shells contain Kummer images only up to inclusions, many constructions only furnish upper bounds rather than equalities; in some contexts (1-column approach) precise equalities can be obtained by fixing arithmetic holomorphic structure. Log-volumes are used to absorb certain indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor-packet construction as multiradial containers
rubrics_metrics.description: For each label collection S±_{j+1} and rational valuation v_Q, form direct sums (over v over v_Q) of log-shells for each prime-strip labeled by * ∈ S±_{j+1}, then take the tensor product over * ∈ S±_{j+1}; the resulting 'tensor-packets' are multiradial mono-analytic containers for actions of splitting monoids and copies of F×_mod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tensor packets are constructed for both holomorphic F-/D-prime-strips and mono-analytic F×μ-/D×μ-prime-strips (Propositions 3.1, 3.2) and are the principal domains on which splitting monoids and labeled copies (F×_mod)^j act; their construction must account for label indeterminacies and be compatible with F±-symmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial algorithms (definition and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiradial algorithms are algorithms that make sense from the point of view of an 'alien arithmetic holomorphic structure' (i.e., related by non-ring horizontal arrows); they are used to construct splitting monoids of LGP-monoids (Theorem A, §3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such algorithms must be canonical enough to minimize log-volume distortion (analogy to Teichmüller theory), must respect the admitted indeterminacies, and produce objects (e.g., splitting monoids) admitting embeddings/actions on tensor packets. Their canonical nature is crucial for later estimates used in IUTchIV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment choice between 0-column and 1-column approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Two modes: 0-column uses log-shells as mono-analytic containers and yields only upper bounds on log-volumes (absorbing indeterminacy via holomorphic hulls); 1-column holds arithmetic holomorphic structure fixed and can yield precise equalities for log-volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection affects how unit-group portions are used (containers vs. documenting device), how indeterminacies are absorbed (holomorphic hulls, log-volumes), and whether one obtains inequalities or equalities in global degree/log-volume results (see §3, Fig. 3.9 and remarks following Theorem 3.11 and Corollary 3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with Θ_LGP-link (multiradial compatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiradial representation and associated Kummer/cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms must be compatible with the Θ_LGP-link (horizontal arrows), i.e., be immune to the (Ẑ)×-indeterminacies acting on O×μ copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compatibility is ensured in part by the multiradiality theory of §2 (mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity) and by construction of cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms for copies of F×_mod (Example 5.1 of [IUTchI]); it is stated as Theorem 3.11 (iii) and summarized in Theorem A (iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Passage to D-prime-strip (forgetting arithmetic holomorphic structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain multiradial representations making sense from an alien arithmetic holomorphic structure, pass from F-prime-strips to D-prime-strips (i.e., forget the vertical arithmetic holomorphic structure), thereby admitting the three indeterminacies (Ind1, Ind2, Ind3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This passage yields the multiradial representation of Theorem 3.11 (i); one must track how indeterminacies act and how Kummer isomorphisms and canonical splittings behave under this forgetting process (discussion in §3).
